title: Cross-provider agent outcome economics
question: What remains of GPT-5.6 and Claude 5 efficiency claims after binding quality, task class, effort, harness, tokens, cache, turns, time, cost, instrument revision, termination, and excluded operational overhead?

inclusion_criteria: Use bounded source segments and retain product, runtime, instrument, and temporal identity.
Prefer official facts, exposed independent methods, primary traces, and explicit counterevidence.
Preserve incomplete operational evidence only in the role and scope it can support.
exclusion_criteria: Do not count dependent retellings as independent origins.
Do not infer model-only traits from product, runtime, transport, quota, or harness symptoms.
Do not compare aggregate scores across instrument revisions as a longitudinal model result.

generality_probe.rationale: A shared current instrument compares two providers and multiple agent variants while the contract remains provider-neutral.

observations.statement: Under Coding Agent Index v1.4, Claude Code with Opus 5 xhigh scored 68 versus Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol max at 65, but Codex led DeepSWE while Claude Code led Terminal-Bench and repository Q&A.

configuration.instrument_revision: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v1.4

outcome.requested: Complete 326 repository, terminal, and software-engineering tasks with three attempts each.
outcome.executed: Published agent variants executed the shared benchmark suite.
outcome.artifact: Patches, terminal outcomes, and repository answers consumed by benchmark verifiers.
outcome.verified: Pass/fail outcomes aggregated per the v1.4 methodology.
outcome.reported: Near aggregate scores conceal different per-evaluation strengths.
outcome.termination: Benchmark attempts completed or failed under harness limits; failure taxonomy is not fully exposed.

confounds: Model, effort, and agent harness all differ; aggregate weighting compresses task-class differences.
configuration_gaps: Exact endpoint snapshots and all attempt trajectories are not exposed in the live comparison.
transfer_limits: Bounded to the two agent variants and v1.4 task distribution; not a model-only or universal ranking.

observations.statement: On the same v1.4 suite, reported pay-per-token API cost averaged $8.17 per task for Claude Code Opus 5 xhigh and $5.00 for Codex GPT-5.6 Sol max.

configuration.instrument_revision: Coding Agent Index v1.4 pooled efficiency metrics

outcome.requested: Measure pay-per-token API spend while attempting the shared benchmark tasks.
outcome.executed: Token usage from benchmark attempts was priced using current provider rates and cache treatment.
outcome.verified: Method includes cached input and cache writes where priced; missing telemetry is excluded rather than zeroed.

average benchmark task-attempt coverage pooled per task

confounds: This excludes infrastructure, engineering, supervision, verifier time, and consumer-plan accounting.
configuration_gaps: Exact endpoint snapshots and all attempt trajectories are not exposed in the live comparison.
transfer_limits: Pay-per-token benchmark cost, not total cost of an accepted production artifact.

observations.statement: Codex GPT-5.6 Sol max averaged 10.2 agent-wall minutes per task versus 23.7 minutes for Claude Code Opus 5 xhigh on the shared v1.4 suite.

configuration.instrument_revision: Coding Agent Index v1.4 execution-time metric

outcome.executed: Agent wall time was pooled over benchmark attempts.
outcome.verified: Method excludes environment startup, verifier, judge, and other harness overhead.

configuration_gaps: Exact endpoint snapshots and all attempt trajectories are not exposed in the live comparison.
transfer_limits: Bounded to active agent time in the published benchmark, not production end-to-end latency.

observations.statement: The current comparison reports 152.1 turns and 21.6M tokens per task for Claude Code Opus 5 xhigh versus 112.3 turns and 13.2M tokens for Codex GPT-5.6 Sol max, while Claude Code had the higher cache-hit rate.

observations.statement: Within Codex on v1.4, moving GPT-5.6 Sol from high to max raised the index from 64 to 65 while cost rose from $3.00 to $5.00, agent time from 6.2 to 10.2 minutes, and tokens from 8.0M to 13.2M per task.

outcome.verified: Same table and instrument; exact endpoint snapshots remain unknown.
outcome.reported: One aggregate point accompanied materially higher resource use.

confounds: Aggregate index can hide per-eval gains and variance; effort may change termination behavior.
configuration_gaps: Exact endpoint snapshots and all attempt trajectories are not exposed in the live comparison.
transfer_limits: A local effort frontier for this task distribution, not a universal recommendation to avoid max.

configuration.instrument_revision: current provider docs plus Coding Agent Index cost method

outcome.verified: Provider prices and benchmark cost definition were captured; no direct billing run was executed.
outcome.reported: Raw provider token prices and measured Cost per Task have distinct denominators.

transfer_limits: Raw rates cannot rank cost per accepted AoA outcome without workload telemetry.

observations.statement: A three-week Claude Code transcript analysis found 85 full-prefix cache rewrites across 13,688 requests; they accounted for 31.3% of all cache-write tokens and affected four Claude model families, indicating a harness/cache cost mechanism rather than a model-specific efficiency trait.

configuration.harness: Claude Code CLI on macOS Darwin 25.5
configuration.instrument_revision: requestId-deduplicated scan of 732 sessions and 13,688 API requests

outcome.requested: Reuse recent conversation-prefix cache entries during long Claude Code work.
outcome.executed: Some consecutive requests rewrote the full prefix instead of reading the recent cache entry.
outcome.artifact: Reporter retained 468MB of transcripts with per-request usage and named request IDs.
outcome.verified: Events were deduplicated by requestId; sub-300-second cases were separated from legitimate >1-hour expiry.
outcome.reported: 85 events used 26.2M cache-write tokens; 25 sub-300-second events represented about 9.3M input-token-equivalents.
outcome.termination: Most work continued, but some session budgets were consumed without proportional generation output.

measurements.notes: Inside even the shortest declared TTL.

confounds: One account, hook configuration, product accounting, and provider cache backend are not independently inspected.
configuration_gaps: Provider billing records, cache backend state, exact client version, and independent reproduction are unavailable.
transfer_limits: Supports a cross-model Claude Code cache pressure; it is not a population incidence or model cost claim.

observations.statement: The v1.4 Cost per Task metric includes pay-per-token input, cache, cache-write, reasoning, and output charges where available, but explicitly excludes infrastructure, engineering, supervision, verifier, and other production overhead.

outcome.requested: Define the economic boundary of published Cost per Task.
outcome.executed: Reviewed methodology and comparison-page metric notes.
outcome.verified: The source explicitly lists included token charges and excluded operational categories.
outcome.reported: Metric is pay-per-token API cost, not total production cost.

configuration_gaps: The amount of excluded overhead is not published for each agent variant.
transfer_limits: Defines interpretation of the benchmark only; it does not estimate total AoA cost.

clusters.label: Agent outcome economics is a vector rather than one model ranking
clusters.supported_scope: Within one current instrument, Opus 5 xhigh has the higher aggregate score while GPT-5.6 Sol max is cheaper, faster, and uses fewer turns and tokens; per-eval leaders also differ.
transfer_limits: One independent benchmark origin and task distribution; both model and harness differ.
unresolved_configuration_gaps: Reliability variance, owner acceptance, supervision cost, and exact endpoint snapshots are not exposed.
clusters.next_action: Select owner utility weights and rerun exact candidate configurations on AoA task classes before choosing a route.

clusters.label: Effort increases have model- and task-specific marginal returns
clusters.supported_scope: The current table exposes different score/cost/time/token slopes across efforts and tiers, so reasoning effort is part of the evaluated configuration rather than a monotonic quality switch.
transfer_limits: Aggregate slopes may differ by per-eval component and production workload.
unresolved_configuration_gaps: Attempt variance and exact termination distributions by effort are unavailable.
clusters.next_action: Run effort sweeps on owner tasks and retain Pareto points rather than one default winner.

clusters.label: Historical and current aggregate scores require revision identity
clusters.supported_scope: The July score 80 and August score 65 belong to different Coding Agent Index revisions and cannot establish a temporal model regression without a frozen common instrument.
transfer_limits: Does not say either published result is wrong.
clusters.next_action: Preserve revision-bound observations and seek same-revision reruns for longitudinal claims.

clusters.label: Token price and benchmark cost omit operational realization pressure
clusters.supported_scope: Provider token prices and benchmark Cost per Task are useful bounded measures, while primary cache traces show product-runtime behavior can add billed work not attributable to model capability or captured by total production-cost accounting.
transfer_limits: The cache issue is one Claude Code corpus and cannot be added numerically to the benchmark rows.
unresolved_configuration_gaps: No shared production workload or full-cost ledger connects the sources.
clusters.next_action: Capture cache categories, retries, supervision, verifier time, termination, and accepted artifacts in owned cost studies.

tensions.label: Higher aggregate score versus lower cost, time, turns, and tokens
tensions.analysis: The outcome and resource axes differ by design; choosing between variants requires an owner utility function and task-class weighting rather than averaging them into confidence.
tensions.remaining_question: What quality delta is worth the additional resource and supervision burden on AoA workloads?

tensions.label: Small aggregate score gain versus large effort-resource increase
tensions.analysis: Both families show non-free effort escalation, but the slopes and per-eval consequences differ; neither supports one universal effort rule.
tensions.remaining_question: Which owner task classes gain enough verified outcome at the higher efforts to justify the cost?

tensions.label: Launch score 80 versus current score 65
tensions.analysis: The historical and current values use different index revisions and comparison populations, so the apparent decline is an instrument discontinuity rather than observed longitudinal regression.
tensions.remaining_question: Can both snapshots be rerun on one frozen v1.4 or later task suite?

tensions.label: High benchmark cache-hit rate versus costly full-prefix rewrite episodes
tensions.analysis: The benchmark reports pooled cache behavior under its harness, while the issue describes intermittent production-client cache misses across a different corpus; both can be true.
tensions.remaining_question: What is the cache-write distribution for the exact AoA harness and session lifecycle?

method_pressures.pressure: Price, cost, time, turns, tokens, cache, quota, and accepted outcomes are repeatedly collapsed into the word efficiency.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Require metric, unit, denominator, exclusions, and task/instrument identity for every economics observation.

method_pressures.pressure: Near aggregate scores conceal different winners across task classes.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Preserve per-evaluation outcomes and owner task weights before any routing recommendation.

method_pressures.pressure: Reasoning effort changes cost and time faster than aggregate score in the captured rows.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Treat effort as configuration and evaluate its local Pareto frontier.

method_pressures.pressure: A live benchmark name survives incompatible task, scoring, and accounting revisions.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Bind every result to an instrument revision and forbid regression claims across revisions without a common rerun.

method_pressures.pressure: Standard pay-per-token benchmark cost excludes runtime anomalies and broader acceptance/supervision overhead.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Add an owned full-outcome ledger before production economics claims; keep external operational traces as replication pressure.

revisit_triggers: Artificial Analysis changes Coding Agent Index revision, task pool, grader, or variant rows.
OpenAI or Anthropic changes token, cache, long-context, or fast-mode pricing.
A common-revision rerun connects the July and August benchmark snapshots.
Owned AoA workload telemetry exposes accepted outcomes, retries, cache writes, supervision, and total wall time.
The cache-rewrite issue receives a confirmed cause, fix, or independent reproduction.
